scope: DCP-LETT-2457A (Whitwell Elwin to John Murray, 3 May 1859), recovered as a third-party source referenced in Darwin's DCP-LETT-2459. Candidate-only research artifact; it does not alter all_letters, packets, primary evidence, ledgers, counts, or exports.

retrieval.retrieval_result: Both endpoints returned non-empty complete records and were saved read-only under this follow-up directory.

source_identity.title: From Whitwell Elwin to John Murray 3 May 1859
source_identity.author: Whitwell Elwin
source_identity.repository: National Library of Scotland (John Murray Archive), Ms. 42197
source_identity.source_role: third-party incoming letter to Murray, intended for forwarding to Darwin
source_identity.source_extent: The HTML contains seven substantive body paragraphs after the salutation, followed by a valediction and a short postscript, with footnotes, bibliography and letter details. The preserved physical item is described as a six-page ALS.

figures.assessment: No inline figure or visual asset is supplied in this record; the evidence is prose, apparatus and metadata.

body_findings.locator: HTML div.body-content, first substantive paragraph after the salutation; source HTML SHA pinned above
body_findings.quote: I have been intending for some days to write to you upon the subject of Mr. Darwin’s work on the Origin of Species.
body_findings.finding: Elwin says that after Murray let him read the manuscript he consulted Sir Charles Lyell, stated his own objections, and was advised by Lyell to convey his impressions to Darwin through Murray. This establishes the letter's immediate subject and a Lyell-mediated route, not a Darwin-authored passage.

body_findings.locator: HTML div.body-content, third substantive paragraph after the salutation
body_findings.quote: The dissertation on species is, on the contrary, in a much harder & drier style. I impute this to the absence of the details.
body_findings.finding: The criticism is about the proposed Origin manuscript's presentation: Elwin thinks omitted natural-history detail weakens both philosophical and popular effect. It is a specific editorial argument, not evidence that Darwin accepted the criticism.

body_findings.locator: HTML div.body-content, fifth substantive paragraph after the salutation
body_findings.quote: Influenced by these considerations Sir Charles urged the publication of Mr. D’s observations upon pigeons
body_findings.finding: Elwin reports Lyell's proposed publication strategy: issue pigeon observations with a brief statement of general principles before the larger natural-history work. The paragraph attributes the recommendation to Lyell and says Elwin agrees; it does not claim that the pigeon book was already sent or published.

body_findings.locator: HTML div.body-content, sixth substantive paragraph after the salutation
body_findings.quote: for an outline it is too much, & for a thorough discussion of the question it is not near enough.
body_findings.finding: Elwin's own strongest formulation is that the present outline is too extensive for an outline but too incomplete for a full treatment. He argues that a pigeon-focused book would be understandable and would prepare the public for the larger work.

body_findings.locator: HTML div.body-content, seventh substantive paragraph after the salutation
body_findings.quote: I write this letter with the intention that you should forward it to Mr. Darwin.
body_findings.finding: The intended route is explicit: Elwin writes to Murray so Murray can forward the note to Darwin. Elwin describes himself as a smatterer and says his aim is to secure fair publication and recognition for Darwin's investigations. This is forwarding evidence, not a direct Elwin-to-Darwin manuscript endpoint.

apparatus_findings: Footnote 1 places Murray's consultation with Elwin after Murray's 10 April communication and identifies Elwin as editor of the Quarterly Review and a close Murray associate.

Footnotes 2 and 4 connect Elwin's account to Lyell's 28/30 March 1859 correspondence and to Lyell's earlier pigeon-publication advice; these are editorial cross-references, not additional Elwin body text.
Footnote 5 states that the letter was sent on to Darwin and points to DCP-LETT-2459. Footnote 6 explains Elwin's title reference to Darwin's Journal of researches.
full_reading.bibliography_findings: The page supplies a bibliography including The Correspondence of Charles Darwin and cited works by Haynes (1916) and Paston (1932). The bibliography was read as apparatus and is not treated as body voice.

evidence.locator: DCP-LETT-2459 HTML div#letter div.body-content, retained body block 1
evidence.quote: As I have thought you perhaps might like to forward the enclosed note to Mr Elwyn I have written it separately.
evidence.finding: Darwin identifies a separate note to Elwin that he asks Murray to forward; this is not evidence that the enclosed note is identical to Elwin's 3 May letter.

evidence.locator: DCP-LETT-2459 HTML div#letter div.body-content, retained body block 2
evidence.quote: It is my deliberate conviction that both Lyells & Mr Elwyns suggestions, (which differ to a certain extent) are impracticable.
evidence.finding: Darwin explicitly evaluates both Lyell's and Elwin's suggestions and calls them impracticable, while thanking both for their kindness. This is direct evidence that Darwin had access to the substance of the forwarded Elwin advice by the 6 May response.

darwin_comparison.editorial_note: DCP-LETT-2459 footnote 1 states that CD's letter to Whitwell Elwin has not been found and was a reply to DCP-LETT-2457A. This confirms the identity of 2457A as the referenced Elwin source, while also confirming that the Darwin-to-Elwin endpoint is missing.

relationship_candidate.source_to_darwin: DCP-LETT-2457A was addressed to Murray and explicitly intended for forwarding; DCP apparatus says it was sent on to Darwin.
relationship_candidate.darwin_use: DCP-LETT-2459 P1-P2 explicitly names Elwin and evaluates his suggestion, so the source is a strong candidate for knowledge available to Darwin before or during the 6 May response.
relationship_candidate.scope: Elwin's critique of the Origin manuscript's detail and his pigeon-first publication recommendation; the whole Elwin letter should not be silently assigned to every later Darwin passage.

date_and_receipt_limits: Elwin's composition date is 3 May 1859 and Darwin's response is dated 6 May [1859].
The apparatus says the Elwin letter was sent on to Darwin, but it does not establish the exact delivery hour or when Darwin read each paragraph.
The surviving Darwin-to-Elwin letter is missing. The separate note Darwin asks Murray to forward in 2459 must not be conflated with the 2457A incoming letter.
negative_boundaries: 2457A is not Darwin voice and cannot be used as an ordinary Darwin target or outgoing transcription.
The Lyell references inside Elwin's letter are reported/quoted editorially and remain attributed to Elwin's account of Lyell, not treated as a newly recovered Lyell-to-Darwin endpoint.
No direct Elwin-to-Darwin manuscript is recovered here; the evidence is an addressed-to-Murray letter plus Darwin's explicit 2459 acknowledgment and the DCP forwarding note.
